Recent duels on this device

Duel Online — direct connection

Your device always shows your own side at the bottom and only your opponent's hand count. The duel itself is always a direct browser-to-browser connection — the only question is how your browsers find each other:

Host a room — one code, no reply

Create a room and share ONE thing: the short room code, or the join link. Your opponent just joins — a public relay introduces your browsers and the connection sets itself up. Nothing is copied back to you.

------

Opponent on a phone? They can scan the join link instead.

Keep this tab open — the room lives here while you wait. The relay only introduces your browsers; after that the duel runs directly between them, same as the code swap below.

Join a room

You are Player 2. Type the room code the host sent you — or open their join link and the code lands here by itself.

Your own relay (optional — the fix for stubborn routers)

Rooms already route through a free public relay when your routers refuse a direct path — that covers most pairs, including two devices on the same Wi-Fi whose router isolates them from each other. If a pair still drops at Connect, a private TURN relay is the reliable answer. Paste credentials below and rooms on this device will use them; they are stored only in this browser, never sent anywhere except to the relay itself when you connect.

Free option: make a free Cloudflare account, open Calls → TURN, create a TURN key, and paste its Token ID and API Token here — the page mints short-lived credentials from them each time you connect. Or paste any static TURN server (URL, username, credential) from another provider.

Fallback — swap codes by hand (no relay involved)

Best-effort, for friendly router pairs: you and your opponent swap two codes (invite, then reply) through Discord or any chat, and your browsers then talk directly. Codes are only produced once network routes finish gathering, so they always carry the full route set — but if both routers block direct paths (the classic drop right at Connect), no code can fix that; use a room above instead.

Engine Duel beta

The Project Ignis duel core (EDOPro's engine, AGPLv3-or-later, via ocgcore-wasm 0.1.4) runs this duel — not the manual table. The engine owns turns, phases, chains, summons, battle and Life Points; card effects resolve from their real CardScripts scripts (AGPLv3-or-later). Pick any two decks: the 36 preloads, or a deck you brought in with “Import .ydk” on the manual table. Scripts for the original 16 preloads ship with the page; scripts for the 20 community preloads — and any other card — load on demand from the full CardScripts corpus pack — chunked by passcode, and only the chunks your two decks actually need are ever downloaded. Hotseat on this device. Banlist enforcement is off. Field rendering: the classic DOM field.

Open source — AGPLv3: this duel runs the Project Ignis core / ocgcore-wasm and the ProjectIgnis/CardScripts corpus, licensed under the GNU AGPLv3-or-later. — every component, its license, its upstream origin, and downloads of the exact bytes this page serves.

Engine duel log

    Duel Puzzles — win this turn

    Fixed boards, your move, one turn to win with only the cards given. There is no timer and no opponent tricks — the other seat plays a quiet dummy turn if you pass, and the puzzle is lost. The rules engine itself is the judge: if the line works, the duel ends.

    Share a puzzle

    Every puzzle below can be copied as a small text block and pasted into Discord. Anyone can import the block here and play the identical board.

    Import a puzzle

    Learn the Table

    Six short lessons, each on a real board with the real engine running it. Every lesson asks its question the way the table will ask it in a live duel — in the second person, at the moment it matters. Stuck on a step? Every step has a “Show me a line” hint.

    Matchup Guides

    Per-matchup lessons in our own words, from our own testing — the cheat sheets, the analyzed tapes, and the sim batches behind the Duelist Cup climb. Every lesson ends with a check-yourself question asked the way the table asks it: in the second person, at the moment it matters. Tap any card chip to read the full card. Nothing here is locked — it’s the community’s table.

    Hand Simulator

    Test opening hands from any deck: deal 5 or 6, redraw, and run 10,000 simulated hands against your chosen starters.

    Road to Worlds — Duelist Cup & the 2027 World Championship

    The World Championship is a TEAM event — teams of three. Here’s how qualifying works, straight from the official event info. The Fire Nation may field a team.

    Duelist Cup: October 2026 (live now)

    • 1st Stage: October 14 – October 25, 2026. Win duels to raise your DLv.
    • Reach DLv. MAX (DLv. 20) to qualify for the 2nd Stage.
    • 2nd Stage: October 23, 00:00 – October 25, 23:59, 2026.
    • Safe climbing: your DLv cannot drop between DLv. 2–15, and once you reach DLv. 17 or DLv. 20 it will never drop below them.
    • Duels in this event have a 300-second time limit.

    2nd Stage: the DP race

    • You earn DP (Duelist Points) for wins; the amount depends on the DP difference between you and your opponent.
    • A win pays at least 1,000 DP with no upper limit. A loss costs at most 1,200 DP, and players at 9,000 DP or less lose a reduced amount.
    • Final ranking is by DP; ties break on number of wins, then number of losses.

    How the World Championship works

    • In each Duelist Cup of the 2027 season, the top-ranked players of the 2nd Stage earn a World Championship Finals Invitation — as team leaders.
    • Season Points are awarded to the top players in the 2nd Stage of each Duelist Cup and in the World Championship Qualifiers, and they add up across the whole 2027 season.
    • Points are earned individually, but team rankings are based on the combined total of all three team members.
    • At the end of the World Championship Qualifiers, the top two teams on points earn the Finals Invitation.
    • You can check Season Points in the game’s Duel Menu under “Season Points.”

    Fire Nation, assemble

    The road to Worlds runs in threes. If you’re grinding the Duelist Cup, find your two teammates, climb together, and stack your Season Points as a team. Talk teams in the Discord.

    About this offer

    What this build contains: the Engine Duel (beta) view runs the Project Ignis duel core (ocgcore, the EDOPro core from edo9300/ygopro-core), compiled to WebAssembly via ocgcore-wasm 0.1.4 (n1xx1/ocgcore-wasm, npm), with card effects resolving from the ProjectIgnis/CardScripts Lua corpus @ commit 3b3a66f685e4c1d0d82214550e56f54c001cc30c. Those components are AGPLv3-or-later; this project’s integration code (the engine worker and the engine UI in this page) is offered under AGPLv3-or-later alongside them. How the corpus chunks were produced: the files under assets/corpus/ are a mechanical re-packaging of the upstream Lua scripts — the corpus (official, pre-release, unofficial, pre-errata, goat, rush and skill scripts) was merged by card passcode with official scripts taking priority, then split into gzipped JSON chunks (pack-0000.json.gz through pack-0186.json.gz) grouped by passcode range, so the page downloads only the chunks a selected deck actually needs. No script logic was rewritten by this re-packaging. The manifest (assets/corpus/pack-manifest.json.gz) enumerates every chunk and its passcodes; the preload subset (assets/engine-scripts.json.gz) holds the original 16 preloaded decks’ scripts in the same format and is not duplicated in the pack. How the card data is packaged: the card database previously shipped as one 5,649,493 B file (card-db.js). It is now split the same way as the corpus: assets/card-index.js (979,426 B) carries every card’s name and play fields and is the only card data loaded at startup, while the full effect text for all 14,759 cards ships as 27 gzipped JSON detail chunks under assets/card-details/ (1,046,802 B gz total), enumerated with SHA-256 hashes in assets/card-details/manifest.json.gz and merged on demand by assets/card-details.js. The split is a mechanical re-packaging: the union of the index and the chunks reproduces the former card-db.js content exactly, card for card and field for field. No card-data binary or chunk is omitted from this offer. Standing offer: the complete Corresponding Source for this build is available at the downloads in the table above, hosted on this page itself. A public GitHub mirror of the source is planned but not yet live; until it is, this page is the source home. The compiled .wasm is a build artifact of the upstream core; its Corresponding Source is the upstream core repository linked in the table.
